brief: True round barn built 1910 by a farmer and his carpenter, about 64 ft across, sided in dark barn-red vertical boards over a low stone base, with tall narrow white-framed windows and louvered vents spaced around the drum and white sliding doors at ground level. The shallow conical shingle roof has a ring of small gabled dormers with round-topped vents and a louvered cupola at the centre. A long gable-roofed shed wing and a small outbuilding join one side; white board fences, a gravel lane and tall spruces surround it, with the gable-roofed farm buildings of the rest of the farm below. (Conical roof; nearest vocabulary roof type is pyramid.)
